summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old man with a history of coronary artery disease, multiple stents, antiphospholipid syndrome, type 2 diabetes, and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction presented with exertional substernal chest pain that was worse than usual. He had no EKG changes or elevated troponins, but due to his high-risk history, he was admitted for observation and treated with IV nitroglycerin and heparin. His chest pain resolved and did not recur. An exercise stress test showed no ischemic changes, supporting stable angina. He was started on isosorbide mononitrate (Imdur) for angina prophylaxis. Aspirin was discontinued due to triple antithrombotic therapy and a history concerning for prior gastrointestinal bleeding. His abdominal pain, which was unrelated to cardiac issues, will continue to be evaluated as an outpatient with a scheduled CT scan. He remained stable, was discharged home on optimized medical therapy, and advised to follow up with cardiology and primary care.
problems: Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery with other forms of angina pectoris
Presence of coronary angioplasty implant and graft
Type 2 diabetes mellitus with unspecified diabetic retinopathy without macular edema
Hypertensive heart disease with heart failure
Personal history of other venous thrombosis and embolism
